options.text: the name of a source program in microcomputers.
set of micro instructions that defines the individual operations in response to a machine language instruction.
a very small segment of machine code.

questions.solution:
(b)
A sequence of microinstructions is called a microprogram, which is stored in a ROM or RAM
called a control memory. Each step in a sequence of steps in the execution of a certain machine
instruction is considered as a microinstruction.

questions.qtext: Which of the following component plays major role in routing data in CPU?
questions.solution:
(c)
A Multiplexer (MUX) is a key component in routing data within the CPU. It selects one of many
input signals and forwards the selected input into a single line, based on control signals.

questions.qtext: Select the correct options regarding different semiconductor memories:

options.text: SRAM uses 6 transistors for storage of one bit.
DRAM uses 2 MOSFETs for storage of one bit.
SRAMs are the main memory of computer systems.

questions.solution:
(a, b)
• DRAMs are slower than SRAMs as it requires periodic refreshing.
• SRAMs are faster and expensive and typically used as the cache memory of computer systems.
• DRAMs are slower but more affordable and typically used as the main memory of computer
systems.
• SRAMs are fabricated using BJT and MOSFET. For storage of 1-bit, 6 transistors are required.
• DRAMs are fabricated using only MOSFET. For storage of 1-bit, 2 MOSFETs are required.

questions.qtext: IEEE standard 754 defined single floating point precision formate uses the excess-bias, then the bias is

options.text: half of centre of exponent range
one less than the half of centre of exponent range
one less than the centre of a exponent range

questions.solution:
(d)
In IEEE 754 single-precision floating-point format, the bias is calculated as
Bias = 2(k – 1) – 1
where k is the number of bits in exponent. Thus, bias is one less than the center of the exponent range.
